device.description: 16-bit single-channel voltage-output DAC (external reference, VSENSE pin) with I2C interface (standard/fast/high-speed), temporary register, read-back and power-down
device.note: dac8571.pdf (SLAS373A) p.2 pin configuration and description, p.3-4 electrical characteristics (VDD 2.7-5.5 V, logic inputs 0.3/0.7 VDD), p.4-5 timing, p.14-15 master write sequence (Table 1), p.16 read sequence (Table 2), p.19 update sequence, address byte (1001 1 A0 0, broadcast 1001 000), control byte, p.20 control byte functionality (Table 5), read-back, p.21-22 examples, power-on reset (zero), p.22-23 power settings (Table 6)

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: DAC register; p.22 power-on reset fills it with zeros (0 V)

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: last control byte C<7:0> (Load1 Load0 = C5 C4, Brcsel = C2, PD0 = C0); sent back third in a read

registers.name: PWR
registers.note: internal: power setting M7 M6 (PD: 00 active, 01 1 kohm, 10 100 kohm, 11 Hi-Z) and M5 (FS: 0 low power, default; 1 fast settling), Table 6

commands.name: BROADCAST LOAD FROM TEMPORARY REGISTER
commands.note: Table 5 broadcast: C5 C4 = 11, C2 = 0: the DAC loads its temporary register (C7 C6 need not be 0)

commands.name: BROADCAST LOAD WITH DATA
commands.note: Table 5 broadcast: C2 = 1, C0 = 0: MS/LS data to the temporary and DAC registers

commands.name: BROADCAST POWER SETTING
commands.in: aa 11 b 1 e 1 pp s x{13}
commands.note: Table 5 broadcast: C2 = 1, C0 = 1: power setting M7-M5 (Table 6)

commands.name: WRITE TEMPORARY REGISTER WITH POWER-DOWN COMMAND
WRITE TEMPORARY REGISTER AND LOAD DAC WITH DATA
commands.note: Table 5: C = 10h; a DAC update leaves the three power-down modes, the low-power/fast-settling setting stays

commands.name: POWER DOWN DAC
commands.note: Table 5: C = 11h, M7-M5 power setting (Table 6: 000 low power, 001 fast settling, 01x 1 kohm, 10x 100 kohm, 11x Hi-Z)

protocol.note: write: address byte, control byte C<7:0>, MS byte, LS byte; executed at the acknowledge after the LS byte. Read: MS byte, LS byte, control byte (Table 2)

pages: p.2 (pins), p.3-4 (VDD 2.7-5.5 V, logic levels), p.4-5 (I2C timing), p.14-16 (write/read sequences, Tables 1-2), p.19-20 (address byte, broadcast address, control byte Table 5, read-back), p.21-22 (examples, power-on reset), p.22-23 (power settings Table 6)
notModeled: analog output, output amplifier, low-power/fast-settling and power-down output loads (PWR stored only; VOUT never driven)
broadcast address 1001 000 (responds regardless of A0): not expressible in the address table; the broadcast control bytes (C5 C4 = 11) are decoded at the part's own address
repeated MS/LS byte pairs after one control byte (each pair updates with the last control byte): the model decodes one control byte and one MS/LS pair per transaction
a power setting written to the temporary register (C = 01h) takes effect only at a later update; the model applies it at once

read-back MS/LS bytes: the datasheet returns the last received I2C MS/LS bytes (discarded data after C = 20h or a broadcast load, power setting bits after a power word); the model returns the temporary register
control bytes with C7/C6 not 0 (outside broadcast) are acknowledged and ignored; other reserved-bit combinations are dropped
address pin A0 is latched at power-up (the model reads it live)
I2C high-speed mode master code and timing limits
variants: dac8571.pdf covers only the DAC8571. DAC7571 (12-bit) and DAC5571/DAC6571 are the simpler single DACs of the family; DAC8574 is the quad I2C version.
